sources.observedFailure: No verifier failure occurred: the visible starter was already a complete solution and passed all 384 scenarios.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Require a starter fatality check before interpreting a clean solve as agent evidence.
validityRisks: The run contains no agent failure and its starter already passes.
extraction.reason: A package leak is a validity repair, not a hard-task candidate.

sources.observedFailure: No verifier failure occurred: the visible starter was already a complete solution and passed all 804 scenarios.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Require a starter fatality check and fresh module state before interpreting a clean solve.
validityRisks: The run contains no agent failure and its starter already passes.
extraction.reason: This is a second instance of the same validity defect, not a prospective candidate.

sources.observedFailure: The subject failed 192 of 339 scenarios because the public specification never quantified sample sufficiency; the passing starter alone contained the value two.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Require every numeric grading threshold and derivation in agent-visible text, then prove the starter fails it.
validityRisks: The preserved root-cause record attributes the failures to package-leak, not capability.
extraction.reason: The isolated cause is precisely what the new contract gate prevents.

sources.observedFailure: The subject failed 32 of 288 only because the host recreated a facade that the public contract promised would retain identity across sessions.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Turn interface lifetime promises into executable host-contract tests before trials.
validityRisks: The preserved root-cause record labels the run harness-contract-violation.
extraction.reason: Harness conformance is a validity control, not task difficulty.

sources.observedFailure: A scheduled backup was absent because of a client/server version mismatch, its alert was lost, and no restore test exposed the failure before both database copies were unavailable.

extraction.transferableMechanism: A backup counts only after an isolated restore and state-digest comparison using compatible tooling.
extraction.subjectActionContract: produce and independently restore-verify one database backup artifact
validityRisks: The historical event has many causes; the task must isolate only restore proof.
extraction.reason: The incident supplies a causal failure, a natural recovery contract, and an isolated state witness.

sources.observedFailure: A valid maintenance command accepted an erroneous removal scope and took multiple subsystems below safe capacity.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Compile destructive work into bounded batches and refuse any batch that crosses a declared subsystem floor.
extraction.subjectActionContract: plan and execute a capacity removal without crossing any subsystem floor
extraction.authorityBoundary: harness-owned live capacity and removal ledger
validityRisks: A fully visible topology may make the task easy even when it is fair.
extraction.reason: The postmortem names both the command defect and the exact bounded-removal remediation.

sources.observedFailure: Deactivating a prefix-list condition broadened a valid BGP policy to every route and redirected roughly half of traffic.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Evaluate the expanded route set and enforce a public maximum-prefix and locality invariant before applying a policy edit.
extraction.subjectActionContract: repair and apply one route policy without broadening its authorized route scope
extraction.authorityBoundary: harness-owned route propagation and traffic ledger
validityRisks: This may be the same causal safety axis as the AWS removal planner despite different domain nouns.
extraction.reason: The exact broadening edit and two concrete safeguards are first-party documented.

sources.observedFailure: A multi-domain path checked one FQDN N times; tests asserted N results and used one-domain integration coverage rather than identity binding.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Bind every current authorization result to its requested principal and grade the external query ledger, not list length.
extraction.subjectActionContract: revalidate every stale domain identity before one certificate issuance decision
extraction.authorityBoundary: harness-owned DNS answers and query-to-domain ledger
validityRisks: The eight-hour rule and every response code must be public; hidden DNS behavior would make the task unfair.
extraction.reason: The incident isolates value-to-identity binding and documents why count-only tests missed it.

sources.observedFailure: No observed incident is claimed; the specification defines digest and size verification before consuming untrusted bytes.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Carry a committed descriptor across retrieval, verify size and digest, then consume only the verified bytes.
extraction.subjectActionContract: fetch and consume the bytes committed by one OCI descriptor
extraction.authorityBoundary: harness-owned mutable registry and consume ledger
validityRisks: There is no prospective observed failure, and the authority recipe may duplicate durable outbox recomputation.
extraction.reason: Exact protocol semantics make contract completion cheap; weak incident support remains explicit.

sources.observedFailure: No observed incident is claimed; KIP-98 defines broker-owned producer ids, epochs, and sequence checks for retry safety.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Use broker-issued epoch and per-partition sequence authority to distinguish retries, gaps, and stale producers.
extraction.subjectActionContract: recover one transactional producer without duplicates, gaps, or stale writes
extraction.authorityBoundary: broker-owned epoch, sequence, transaction log, and committed records
validityRisks: The mechanism overlaps the existing uncertain-effect and exactly-once families.
extraction.reason: Protocol-only support ranked below six sources with incidents or a simpler exact protocol.

sources.observedFailure: No observed incident is claimed; finalizers coordinate irreversible object deletion with controller-owned cleanup.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Remove a finalizer only after authoritative external cleanup succeeds, while retries preserve liveness.
extraction.subjectActionContract: reconcile deletion and release a finalizer only after external cleanup
extraction.authorityBoundary: API-server object state plus external provider resource ledger
validityRisks: The task may collapse to the deployment rollback family or expose its witness through normal provider reads.
extraction.reason: Protocol-only support and likely family overlap ranked below the six drafting attempts.

sources.observedFailure: No observed incident is claimed; force-unlock requires the unique lock id so one caller cannot release another writer's lock.

extraction.transferableMechanism: Carry the backend-issued lock nonce and refuse a force-unlock unless it names the exact current failed lock.
extraction.subjectActionContract: recover one failed state lock without unlocking a concurrent writer
extraction.authorityBoundary: backend-owned current lock id, owner, state serial, and unlock ledger
validityRisks: No observed failure supports prospective difficulty and the stable-token recipe may not be novel.
extraction.reason: The protocol exposes an exact nonce rule and a structurally separate backend witness.
